obernants.operator: Given (g,x,y), reconstruct all u64 pairs (a,b) satisfying E(a,b)=(g,x,y). Necessarily ax+by=g and gcd(a,b)=g, but those conditions alone do not enforce the coefficient policy. For g=0 only (0,0) with x=y=0 qualifies; (g,1,0) for g>0 can admit several b. Preserve the recurrence constraint and ambiguity.

obernants.operator: For a returned g>0, divisibility of a and b by g plus ax+by=g establishes greatest common divisor over integers: every common divisor divides the displayed combination. Runtime evaluates no potentially large input-coefficient products. Tests check their products with checked i128 operations.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Conditional mathematical model with bounded correspondence evidence, not a formal proof.
obernants.assumptions: Standard Rust arithmetic and trustworthy independent oracle; resource assumptions stated in the model.
obernants.domain: u64 inputs; integer coefficients and explicit finite-machine projection premises.
obernants.operator: For (a,b)!=(0,0), let E(a,b)=(g,x0,y0). All integer solutions to ax+by=g are exactly x=x0+k*(b/g), y=y0-k*(a/g), k in Z. This describes certificate solutions, not the graph of the deterministic coefficient policy: only k=0 is returned. For (0,0), every integer coefficient pair solves the equation but only (0,0) is returned. Arbitrary k and products require mathematical integers or checked arithmetic; i128 is not a universal family domain.

obernants.domain: u64 inputs; integer coefficients and explicit finite-machine projection premises.
obernants.operator: For g>0, positive d divides both a and b iff d divides g. Thus g is the greatest common divisor in the divisibility order and ax+by=c has an integer solution iff g divides c. Sufficiency scales the returned certificate by c/g; necessity follows by divisibility of every linear combination. At (0,0), only c=0 is solvable, and every positive d divides both inputs; no finite positive maximum exists.

obernants.domain: u64 inputs; integer coefficients and explicit finite-machine projection premises.
obernants.operator: For modulus m>=2 and a:u64, gcd(a,m)=1 iff a has an inverse modulo m. The unique representative r in [0,m) is E(a,m).x rem_euclid m. Other Bezout solutions project to the same r. No inverse is inferred when gcd>1; modulus zero is undefined and modulus one is excluded. For verification convert a,r,m to u128: a*r fits u128 for u64 operands; the same product may overflow i128 even though the signed coefficient identity is safe.
